summaryZh: Ferguson 实验室研究泛素信号如何塑造神经发育中的染色质与基因调控，并研究溶酶体信号异常引发的神经炎症和神经退行性变化。研究使用条件性小鼠模型、行为分析、CUT&RUN、ATAC-seq 和转录组学。
researchQuestions: 泛素修饰与清除染色质调控蛋白如何影响神经元成熟？
溶酶体信号异常如何驱动神经炎症？
topics: 神经炎症与神经退行性变化

evidence.quote: Ferguson Lab at UC San Diego
Ferguson Lab at UC San Diego

Our lab is breaking new ground in understanding the epigenetic mechanisms that control neurodevelopment, and we have opened a new (if so far very small) field of study on the unexpected role of ubiquitin signaling in shaping chromatin. In other lines of investigation, we are studying neuroinflammation in the context of neurodegeneration (in the brain and the eye).

Because complete loss of BAP1 is embryonic-lethal, we recently generated conditional mouse models removing BAP1 from excitatory neurons of the forebrain or cerebellum, and paired behavioral analyses with CUT&RUN, ATAC-seq, and transcriptomics.

Borrowing the proteomic strategy that had worked for the APC, I applied unbiased proteomics to the lysosome with Steve Gygi (Harvard) and Brandon Gassaway (BYU), quantifying more than 10,000 brain proteins to define the full set of PI(3,5)P₂-dependent lysosomal substrates—and found that lysosomal failure drives hyperactivation of innate immunity.

After starting my lab at UCSD, we realized that we had found not a single, especially important substrate but a general principle: the canonical mitotic regulators—Ki-67, the chromosome-passenger complex (CPC) and its kinase Aurora B, and topoisomerase 2α—are all normally ubiquitinated to be cleared from neurons as they exit mitosis and differentiate (Ledvin et al., Developmental Cell , 2023).
